    Heredity of C(D) (Proposition 4.4, Eⁿ = 0 for n ≥ 2) #

    Split an object M into the summand M_A formed by its entries A i and the summand M_R of its other entries, so that 1_M = ι_A π_A + ι_R π_R. By (4.1), E(M_A, -) = 0 and E(-, M_R) = 0. A generator of Eⁿ(C, A) with n ≥ 2 is α ⊗ w with α ∈ E(M, A) and w a word starting in E(-, M). Then α = (π_R)^*(ι_R)^* α, and by balance α ⊗ w ≡ (ι_R)^* α ⊗ (π_R)_* w, whose second word starts in E(-, M_R) = 0. So Eⁿ = 0 for all n ≥ 2 (Gorsky, Nakaoka and Palu).
